name: ams1117_smoke
description: One datasheet-extract block on a page of its own: the first real-host test of synthesised anchors. The block carries no geometry, so the assembler names every pin endpoint itself — a one-cell stub and a flag on each rail endpoint, a net label on each signal endpoint. What a human has to judge here is whether that reads as a schematic: three parts, eight flags (U1's tab pin 4 is a second VOUT endpoint, so VCC anchors three times), and no wire that is not an anchor stub.

provenance.note: Not a product page — a readability probe. It exists so the synthesised anchors can be looked at on a real canvas before six more blocks are written on the strength of the rule.

blocks.note: Centred by hand so the synthesised anchors have room to be read. The block's own layout is the signed author's placement and is not re-solved.
